findings.claim: The loop-4 fix sets animation: none inline with importance on the checklist and both tags while measuring. That removes every CSS animation, including one whose values hold for good (animation-fill-mode forwards, or an infinite iteration count), so the test now measures a page the learner never sees. Reproduced on a git archive of a942501c with the private completed work plus one added rule each: (a) a forwards-filled keyframes animation that holds .pack-tag-day at another width passes all 12 tests; at 3d48ec9a the same variant failed task 11; (b) an infinite keyframes animation that scales both tags passes all 12; at 3d48ec9a it failed task 11; (c) a forwards-filled animation that holds .pack-tag-overnight's padding at another size passes all 12. In each case the unmodified page, opened in the same pinned Chromium at 1280x1000 and read after 300ms, draws the tag not 200px wide or with padding other than 12px. So README line 17 ('It rejects scaling, rotating, translating or zooming a tag') and the task 11 Outcome (line 141, 'exactly 200px wide on screen') are false for an animated tag, and earlier concern 2 (scale changing the drawn size) recurs through animations. Only lab.json notes say animations are switched off. Medium, graded like cl3-sme-005: a wrong page passes, but only after a deliberate keyframes rule, and the calculated width is still measured, so the calculation is not skipped. The transition half of the fix is sound: a transition never changes the settled value, and setting transition-property to none cancels a running one, so it cannot hide a lasting error (the only exception found is a @starting-style entry transition with an absurd duration, which is not worth handling). Removing animations also has a real benefit to keep: a harmless 2s entrance animation (translate plus opacity, no fill) failed task 11 at 3d48ec9a when measured mid-flight and passes now.

evidence.section: 6.1 Cascade Sorting Order (Origin and Importance: animation declarations sit above normal author declarations and below important author declarations)
animation-fill-mode: forwards (after the animation ends it keeps applying the values from the time it ended)
3. Starting of transitions (a running transition with no matching transition-property value must be cancelled)

findings.recommendation: Keep transition: none. Drop animation from the neutralised list. Once transitions are off, go through el.getAnimations() for the checklist and both tags: call finish() on each finite animation, so a forwards fill is measured at its end values and a no-fill animation simply goes away. Fail with a plain message (a repeating animation changes the tag's size) when an infinite animation's keyframes touch width, min/max-width, inline-size, padding, border, margin, box-sizing, transform, scale, rotate, translate or zoom. A prototype of exactly this, run in this critic's work dir against the full suite, failed task 11 on variants (a), (b) and (c). It passed all 12 on the completed work, the 2s entrance animation, an infinite background-colour animation, and the transition variants (checklist transition: all, interpolate-size with tag width transitions, 5s all-property transitions). Then update the lab.json notes phrase about animations and add an animation-held variant to the solved-run matrix.

findings.claim: The pinned() map resets transform, scale, rotate, translate and zoom on .site-aside itself with inline !important, so scaling the checklist is invisible to the rendered-width check ('something around it is scaling it'), which only catches ancestors above the checklist. Reproduced: the completed work plus a zoom on .site-aside passes all 12 tests at both a942501c and 3d48ec9a, while the real page draws both tags not 200px wide. A scale on .site-aside also passes task 11 (tasks 5 and 6 catch it). A zoom on the outer .page wrapper, which is not pinned, does fail task 11, though with the misleading 'border area is not 3px' message. This predates loop 4 (those pin entries are unchanged context in the 3d48ec9a..a942501c diff). Low: an unlikely edit, and the calculated width is still required.
findings.recommendation: Before pinning, read .site-aside's computed transform, scale, rotate, translate and zoom, after any animations are settled as in cl4-sme-001. Fail with a checklist-specific message when they are not none and 1, as the tags' unscaled check already does. Alternatively, take one rendered-width reading of each tag before the pin is applied.

findings.claim: The new own-layout cause prints the tag's computed display. A floated or absolutely positioned box is blockified, so its computed display is 'block'. For those two causes the learner reads '... the tag itself is not an ordinary block (its display is block, or it is floated or absolutely positioned) ...', which sounds self-contradictory. Reproduced: floated tags and absolutely positioned tags (with or without insets inside a positioned checklist) both fail on the control with 'its display is block'. Inline-block and table tags print their real display correctly. The outcome is right and float and positioning are still named, so this is message polish.

evidence.section: 2.7 Automatic Box Type Transformations (blockification sets the computed outer display type to block)

findings.recommendation: Build the cause from the reason that was actually detected: name the display only when it starts with inline or table; otherwise say 'it is floated' (cs.float is not none) or 'it is absolutely positioned' (cs.position is absolute or fixed).

The windows are now 800x800 and 1280x1000 (lines 124-127), so vw, vh, vmin and vmax each resolve differently between runs. Reproduced on the full suite: a .pack-tag-overnight width in vh that equals 200px at the 800px-high window, the same in vmin, and the same in vw at the 800px-wide window each fail task 11 alone, on the layout width at 1280x1000. Troubleshooting now says a width that depends on the window's width or height fails, which holds for single-unit widths. Theoretical residue only: any two-size sample can be met by a calc that mixes vw and vh with opposite signs, and that is not a plausible learner edit.
